## Key invariants

### `INV-S3-ONLY`

> maragudb is an embedded Go SQL database. Its only durable state is in S3-compatible object storage.

- `internal/engine` `TestTx_Commit/a_commit_from_another_process_is_visible_to_a_transaction_begun_after_it`: a transaction in another process sees a commit acknowledged before it began, read from the store
- `internal/sim` `TestSimulator/corpus_finds_no_anomalies`: the fixed corpus, with injected errors, latency, lost acknowledgements, outages, and crashes, finds no anomalies with any checker and exercises every fault

### `INV-MULTI-WRITER`

> Many processes can read and write the same database at the same time, with strict serializable ACID transactions.

- `internal/engine` `TestEngine_MatchesModel/transactions_over_several_processes_with_compaction_and_GC_behave_like_a_map`: random transactions over several processes, with compaction and GC, behave like a map
- `internal/sim` `TestSimulator/corpus_finds_no_anomalies`: the fixed corpus, with injected errors, latency, lost acknowledgements, outages, and crashes, finds no anomalies with any checker and exercises every fault
- `internal/sim` `TestSimulator/every_checker_passes_with_the_lease_working,_disabled,_and_overlapping`: every checker passes with background maintenance under a working lease, without the lease, and with overlapping leases

### `INV-CACHE-LOSS`

> Caches in memory and on local disk are allowed (in the style of turbopuffer), but correctness never depends on them: losing every cache never loses or corrupts data.

- `internal/engine` `TestDB_Stats/a_stale_disk-cached_manifest_is_refreshed_on_open`: a stale manifest in the disk cache is replaced by the store's newer one on open
- `internal/sim` `TestSimulator/corpus_finds_no_anomalies`: the fixed corpus, with injected errors, latency, lost acknowledgements, outages, and crashes, finds no anomalies with any checker and exercises every fault

### `INV-REGISTER`

> API: a database/sql driver, registered explicitly with maragudb.RegisterDriver(maragudb.Options{...}). There is no init registration.

- `.` `TestRegisterDriver/registers_under_the_given_name_and_opens_with_sql.Open`: RegisterDriver registers the driver explicitly under a name, and sql.Open with an s3://bucket/prefix DSN works

### `INV-OPTIONS`

> API: Options use pointer fields with opinionated defaults, as in <https://github.com/maragudk/sqlite/blob/main/sqlite.go>.

- `internal/engine` `TestOpen/defaults_to_a_memory_cache_and_a_one_hour_grace_period`: options left unset get their defaults: a memory cache and a one hour grace period

### `INV-DSN`

> API: The DSN identifies a bucket and a prefix, for example s3://bucket/prefix.

- `.` `TestRegisterDriver/registers_under_the_given_name_and_opens_with_sql.Open`: RegisterDriver registers the driver explicitly under a name, and sql.Open with an s3://bucket/prefix DSN works
- `.` `TestRegisterDriver/rejects_a_bad_DSN_when_connecting`: DSNs that are not s3://bucket/prefix fail with ErrDSN
- `internal/sqldriver` `TestParseDSN`: s3://bucket/prefix DSNs parse into a bucket and a prefix, and malformed DSNs are rejected

### `INV-PLACEHOLDERS`

> API: Placeholders use the $1 style.

- `.` `TestDB/gives_a_parameter_the_type_of_its_context,_as_Postgres_does`: a string parameter is read like a quoted literal of the type its context gives it, an int64 converts to a double precision, and a conversion that a Postgres driver might make differently is ErrUnsupported
- `.` `TestDB/round_trips_every_type_through_parameters_and_Scan`: every type and NULL round-trips through $1-style parameters and Scan
- `internal/pgdiff` `TestParameters/a_parameter_of_every_Go_type_in_every_context_gives_the_same_result_as_Postgres_with_pgx,_or_is_rejected_as_unsupported`: hegel-drawn Go values bound as parameters in contexts that infer different types give the same result or error class as Postgres with pgx, or fail on both when pgx refuses to encode them, unless maragudb rejects them as unsupported
- `internal/sql/exec` `TestSession_Insert/binds_parameters_of_every_type`: every type binds through a parameter, and a timestamptz keeps microseconds
- `internal/sql/exec` `TestSession_Select/gives_parameters_the_type_of_their_context`: a parameter of a Go type other than string converts to the type its context infers, overflows like an integer in an integer context, and is ErrUnsupported where it cannot convert

### `INV-STATS`

> API: A small native API exposes Stats(), with S3 request counts by kind and cache hits and misses, and also exposes cache options.

- `.` `TestStats/counts_requests_and_cache_hits_across_connections`: Stats reports request counts by kind and cache hits across connections
- `internal/engine` `TestDB_Stats/counts_cache_hits_and_misses_per_tier`: Stats counts memory and disk cache hits and misses

### `INV-CAS-COMMIT`

> Concurrency: multi-writer with optimistic concurrency. Commits are compare-and-swap writes through S3 conditional writes (If-Match / If-None-Match). No external lock service is used.

- `internal/engine` `TestEngine_MatchesModel/conflicting_commits_from_two_processes_leave_exactly_one_winner`: of two random conflicting commits from two processes, exactly one wins
- `internal/engine` `TestTx_Commit/concurrent_write_transactions_conflict_and_the_loser's_writes_are_not_applied`: of two concurrent write transactions on different keys, the second commit gets ErrConflict and none of its writes are applied
- `internal/s3` `TestAWSClient_Tigris/conditional_writes_and_reads_behave_like_the_fake`: on Tigris, If-None-Match, If-Match, conditional and ranged reads, list, and delete behave like the fake, and the PUT ETag equals the GET ETag; latencies are recorded
- `internal/s3fake` `TestClient_Put/fails_with_ErrPreconditionFailed_when_IfMatch_does_not_match`: the fake refuses a conditional write whose ETag does not match, as S3 does

### `INV-STRICT-SERIALIZABLE`

> Isolation: strict serializable. A read transaction sees every commit that was acknowledged before the transaction started.

- `internal/engine` `TestTx_Commit/a_commit_from_another_process_is_visible_to_a_transaction_begun_after_it`: a transaction in another process sees a commit acknowledged before it began, read from the store
- `internal/history` `TestCheckListAppend`: the list-append checker accepts serializable histories and rejects stale reads, write skew, lost updates, reads of failed writes, duplicate values, and cycles through real-time edges
- `internal/sim` `TestSimulator/corpus_finds_no_anomalies`: the fixed corpus, with injected errors, latency, lost acknowledgements, outages, and crashes, finds no anomalies with any checker and exercises every fault

### `INV-DB-CONFLICTS`

> Isolation: In section 1, conflict detection is at database granularity: any concurrent write commit is a conflict.

- `.` `TestTx/an_explicit_transaction_returns_ErrConflict,_which_IsRetryable,_and_a_retry_succeeds`: an explicit transaction that loses to a concurrent commit returns ErrConflict, which errors.Is and IsRetryable detect, and a retry succeeds
- `internal/engine` `TestDB_Tigris/concurrent_writers_conflict_and_retry_until_every_write_lands`: on Tigris, concurrent writers conflict and retry until every write is in the database
- `internal/engine` `TestEngine_MatchesModel/conflicting_commits_from_two_processes_leave_exactly_one_winner`: of two random conflicting commits from two processes, exactly one wins
- `internal/engine` `TestTx_Commit/concurrent_write_transactions_conflict_and_the_loser's_writes_are_not_applied`: of two concurrent write transactions on different keys, the second commit gets ErrConflict and none of its writes are applied

### `INV-AUTOCOMMIT-RETRY`

> Isolation: A single statement outside an explicit transaction retries automatically on conflict.

- `.` `TestTx/a_statement_outside_a_transaction_retries_on_conflict`: an autocommit statement that conflicts retries by itself and succeeds
- `internal/sql/exec` `TestSession_Transactions/a_transaction_sees_a_snapshot,_and_an_explicit_transaction_gets_ErrConflict_while_autocommit_retries`: an explicit transaction that loses gets ErrConflict, while the same statement in autocommit retries and succeeds
- `internal/sql/exec` `TestSession_Transactions/autocommit_retries_a_conflict_caused_by_a_concurrent_commit_during_the_statement`: an autocommit statement that conflicts with a commit made during it retries and applies once

### `INV-RETRYABLE-ERROR`

> Isolation: An explicit transaction returns a typed, retryable serialization error, similar to Postgres SQLSTATE 40001. Callers detect it with errors.Is or errors.As.

- `.` `TestTx/an_explicit_transaction_returns_ErrConflict,_which_IsRetryable,_and_a_retry_succeeds`: an explicit transaction that loses to a concurrent commit returns ErrConflict, which errors.Is and IsRetryable detect, and a retry succeeds
- `internal/sql/exec` `TestSession_Transactions/a_transaction_sees_a_snapshot,_and_an_explicit_transaction_gets_ErrConflict_while_autocommit_retries`: an explicit transaction that loses gets ErrConflict, while the same statement in autocommit retries and succeeds

### `INV-READ-ONLY`

> Isolation: Read-only transactions never conflict.

- `.` `TestTx/a_read-only_transaction_never_conflicts_and_rejects_writes`: a read-only transaction commits despite a concurrent commit and rejects writes
- `internal/engine` `TestTx_Commit/read-only_transactions_never_conflict`: a read-only transaction commits after a concurrent write commit
- `internal/sql/exec` `TestSession_Transactions/read-only_transactions_reject_writes_and_DDL`: a read-only transaction rejects INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, and DDL

### `INV-DURABLE-ACK`

> Durability: a commit is acknowledged only after its S3 write is confirmed.

- `internal/engine` `TestTx_Commit/a_commit_returns_ErrCommitUnknown_when_the_store_stops_answering_after_the_write`: a commit whose manifest write is never confirmed is not acknowledged and returns ErrCommitUnknown

### `INV-PG-SUBSET`

> SQL flavor: a strict subset of Postgres 18. The same SQL text runs on both, and for every statement that maragudb accepts, the result is identical to Postgres: rows, values, column names, affected-row counts, and transaction state. When Postgres fails a statement, maragudb fails it too, with the same error class wherever the error does not depend on evaluation order or physical row order. The only exceptions are the differences that docs/unsupported.md lists with a DEV- ID, an example, and a test each. There is one: DEV-20, where Postgres scans the whole table and fails on a row that the primary key condition does not select, and maragudb does not fail.

- `.` `TestTx/a_statement_that_does_not_parse_aborts_the_transaction,_as_in_Postgres`: a syntax error or an unsupported statement in an explicit transaction aborts it, so a later commit rolls everything back
- `internal/pgdiff` `TestCasts/every_value_casts_to_every_type_the_same_as_Postgres,_or_is_rejected_as_unsupported`: hegel-drawn values of every supported type, and integer and numeric literals, cast to every supported type and back to text with the same result or error class as Postgres, unless maragudb rejects the cast as unsupported
- `internal/pgdiff` `TestCasts/text_casts_to_every_type,_and_back_to_text,_the_same_as_Postgres,_or_are_rejected_as_unsupported`: hegel-drawn text near valid input for bigint, double precision, boolean, bytea, and timestamptz casts to the type and back to text with the same result or the same error class as Postgres, unless maragudb rejects it as unsupported
- `internal/pgdiff` `TestChecks/checks_CHECK_constraints_in_the_order_of_their_names,_after_NOT_NULL_and_before_the_keys,_as_Postgres_does`: an INSERT or UPDATE evaluates the NOT NULL constraints, then the CHECK constraints in the order of their names, failing at the first that is false or fails itself, and then the primary key and the unique indexes, row by row, so it fails with the same class as Postgres, and NULL passes a CHECK
- `internal/pgdiff` `TestChecks/names_CHECK_constraints_as_Postgres_does,_and_fails_a_CHECK_as_Postgres_does_when_the_table_is_created`: CHECK constraints get Postgres's names, after the one column they read or after the table, numbered past the names of every constraint of every table, they share the names of a table's constraints with its PRIMARY KEY and UNIQUE constraints and its NOT NULL constraints, and a CHECK that is not boolean, reads a missing column, or repeats a name fails with the class of Postgres's error
- `internal/pgdiff` `TestDefaults/fills_in_defaults_as_Postgres_does,_with_the_same_errors`: a column's DEFAULT is used for a column that an INSERT leaves out, for DEFAULT in VALUES and in SET, and for DEFAULT VALUES, converted to the column's type by assignment, and a DEFAULT that reads a column, has a parameter, has the wrong type, or fails to fold fails as in Postgres
- `internal/pgdiff` `TestForeignKeys/cascades_through_chains_of_tables_and_trees,_and_rejects_actions_whose_outcome_depends_on_their_order`: ON DELETE CASCADE, SET NULL, and SET DEFAULT go through chains of tables and down self-referencing trees as in Postgres, the rows they change are checked like any other, and a DELETE whose actions could give another outcome in another order is rejected
- `internal/pgdiff` `TestForeignKeys/checks_a_self-referencing_table_at_the_end_of_the_statement,_as_Postgres_does`: a self-referencing table is checked at the end of each statement, so an UPDATE that moves parents and children together passes, one that moves only the parents fails, a cycle of references can be inserted in one statement, and deleting a whole tree passes where deleting part of it fails
- `internal/pgdiff` `TestForeignKeys/checks_foreign_keys_and_fires_their_actions_as_Postgres_does`: an insert or update of a row whose foreign key has no NULL and no parent row fails with 23503 at the end of the statement, a delete or key update of a referenced row fails with 23503 for NO ACTION and 23001 for RESTRICT, or deletes, sets to NULL, or sets to the defaults the referencing rows, with the rows the same on both afterwards
- `internal/pgdiff` `TestForeignKeys/creates_and_drops_foreign_keys_as_Postgres_does,_with_the_same_names_and_errors`: FOREIGN KEY and REFERENCES get Postgres's names, reference a primary key or the first unique index on the referenced columns, fail with the class of Postgres's error for a missing table or column, columns without a unique index, a different number of columns, and incompatible types, and DROP TABLE and DROP INDEX of what a foreign key depends on fail with 2BP01
- `internal/pgdiff` `TestIndexConditions/evaluates_the_other_conditions_only_on_the_rows_that_the_primary_key_conditions_select,_as_Postgres_does_with_an_index_scan`: with sequential scans off, Postgres evaluates the other WHERE conditions only on the rows that the conditions on the primary key index select: comparisons and IN of constants on any key column, a boolean key column, and key equalities implied by equalities with a constant; maragudb accepts such statements and gives the same results
- `internal/pgdiff` `TestIndexConditions/takes_the_index_conditions_out_of_an_OR_as_Postgres_does_when_it_drops_constants_and_common_conditions_from_the_OR`: in a WHERE clause, Postgres drops the arguments of an OR that are FALSE or NULL constants and takes the conditions common to every argument out of the OR, which can make them index conditions; maragudb does the same and gives the same results
- `internal/pgdiff` `TestIndexPlans/Postgres_takes_the_certain_conditions_on_an_indexed_column_as_conditions_of_the_scan_of_the_index,_and_picks_between_indexes`: EXPLAIN on Postgres 18 with sequential scans off shows that comparisons, IN, and boolean conditions on any column of a secondary index are conditions of its scan, that it picks between the primary key and another index with conditions, and that it scans a whole index in order for ORDER BY
- `internal/pgdiff` `TestIndexPlans/evaluates_the_other_conditions_only_on_the_rows_that_every_index_scan_Postgres_could_pick_skips,_and_otherwise_on_every_row`: with several indexes, a condition that can fail is evaluated on the rows that any index scan Postgres could pick reads: those of each index's certain conditions, and every row when an index without them could serve a condition or ORDER BY; maragudb gives Postgres's result when every such scan agrees, and rejects the statement otherwise
- `internal/pgdiff` `TestIndexes/enforces_UNIQUE_as_Postgres_does,_with_NULLs_distinct_or_not,_and_fails_a_unique_index_on_duplicated_rows`: inserts, updates, and CREATE UNIQUE INDEX that would give two rows the same values of a unique index fail with SQLSTATE 23505 on both, NULLs collide only with NULLS NOT DISTINCT, and the rows are the same on both afterwards
- `internal/pgdiff` `TestIndexes/fails_a_cycle_of_unique_values_in_an_UPDATE_as_Postgres_does_in_every_order,_and_rejects_a_chain`: an UPDATE whose rows swap the values of a unique index or of the primary key fails with SQLSTATE 23505 on both, an UPDATE that moves a chain of rows onto the values the next one leaves is rejected, and one that moves rows onto free values succeeds on both
- `internal/pgdiff` `TestIndexes/names_indexes_as_Postgres_does,_in_the_namespace_of_tables,_with_the_same_errors`: CREATE INDEX, DROP INDEX, and UNIQUE constraints name their indexes as Postgres does, tables and indexes share one namespace, and every clash, missing name, and wrong kind of relation fails with the class of Postgres's error
- `internal/pgdiff` `TestParameters/a_parameter_of_every_Go_type_in_every_context_gives_the_same_result_as_Postgres_with_pgx,_or_is_rejected_as_unsupported`: hegel-drawn Go values bound as parameters in contexts that infer different types give the same result or error class as Postgres with pgx, or fail on both when pgx refuses to encode them, unless maragudb rejects them as unsupported
- `internal/sql/exec` `TestSession_Defaults/now()_is_the_start_of_the_transaction,_the_same_for_every_use_in_it,_from_the_engine's_clock_at_microsecond_precision`: now(), CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, and transaction_timestamp() are the start of the transaction on the engine's clock, truncated to microseconds, the same in every statement of a transaction and in a DEFAULT, and later in a later transaction
- `internal/sql/exec` `TestSession_Insert/applies_Postgres's_assignment_casts`: an INSERT applies the assignment casts Postgres has: a quoted literal as the column's type, numeric and float literals rounded into bigint, integers widened to double precision, and any value written into text
- `internal/sql/exec` `TestSession_Select/accepts_a_WHERE_clause_only_when_its_outcome_is_the_same_in_every_order_Postgres_could_pick_on_the_rows_its_primary_key_index_selects`: a WHERE clause whose outcome on a row depends on the order Postgres evaluates its conditions in, including the equalities its equivalence classes imply, is ErrUnsupported, and so is a LIKE on a key column that can fail; the other conditions are evaluated only on the rows that the primary key conditions select, and every other WHERE clause fails exactly when Postgres fails in every order
- `internal/sql/exec` `TestSession_Select/does_not_fold_the_stable_conversions_between_timestamptz_and_text,_as_Postgres_does_not,_and_rejects_one_that_can_fail`: a conversion between timestamptz and text is evaluated when the statement runs, so a CASE does not prune on it and a WHERE condition on it is evaluated once before rows are read, and one without columns that can fail is ErrUnsupported
- `internal/sql/exec` `TestSession_Select/evaluates_expressions_like_Postgres`: expressions evaluate as in Postgres: integer literals are 32-bit, numeric literals adapt to double precision, quoted literals take the type their context demands, || writes any type next to text, and casts use Postgres's text formats
- `internal/sql/exec` `TestSession_Select/follows_Postgres_in_the_details_of_analysis`: an IN whose constant elements have no common type compares them one at a time, a CASE operand of unknown type is text, +1 in ORDER BY is no position, ORDER BY a name is ambiguous only between different expressions, and a read-only transaction reports analysis errors before it refuses a write
- `internal/sql/exec` `TestSession_Transactions/a_failed_statement_aborts_the_transaction_until_it_ends,_as_in_Postgres`: after a failed statement every statement of the transaction fails with ErrTxAborted, COMMIT rolls it back, and ROLLBACK ends it
- `internal/sql/exec` `TestSession_Unique/rejects_a_row_whose_values_another_row_has,_in_one_statement_or_across_statements,_and_allows_NULLs`: inserts and updates that would give two rows the same non-NULL values of a unique index fail with ErrDuplicateKey, within one statement, across statements of a transaction, and against committed rows, and NULLs never collide unless NULLS NOT DISTINCT
- `internal/sql/exec` `TestSession_Update/moves_rows_when_the_primary_key_changes,_and_rejects_a_move_whose_outcome_depends_on_row_order`: an UPDATE of primary key columns succeeds or fails as in Postgres in every row order, and a chain of rows that move onto keys that other rows move away from is ErrUnsupported, and a cycle of them ErrDuplicateKey
- `internal/sqllogictest` `TestRegressions/NOT_of_a_comparison_of_an_expression_with_itself_is_NULL_where_the_expression_is`: the statements of the sqllogictest corpus that found differences from Postgres give the same results on both sides

### `INV-UNSUPPORTED`

> SQL flavor: maragudb is stricter than Postgres only through ErrUnsupported, SQLSTATE 0A000 (feature_not_supported), whose message says what is unsupported and, where possible, what to write instead. Every class of statement it rejects is listed in docs/unsupported.md.

- `internal/sql/exec` `TestSession_Select/rejects_what_Postgres_accepts_only_with_ErrUnsupported`: the numeric type, bit strings, non-ISO timestamps, LIKE on bytea, and the other rejections of accepted Postgres SQL are ErrUnsupported with a hint

### `INV-INT-OVERFLOW`

> Types: bigint int8 64-bit integer. Overflow is an error.

- `.` `TestDB/reports_statement_errors_with_errors.Is`: statement errors, including int overflow as ErrOutOfRange, are detectable with errors.Is
- `internal/sql/exec` `TestSession_Select/reports_evaluation_errors_like_Postgres`: integer and bigint overflow in +, -, *, /, unary minus, and abs is ErrOutOfRange, at 32 bits for integer literals, among the other evaluation errors

### `INV-TYPES`

> Types: As in Postgres, an integer literal that fits in 32 bits has type integer, and arithmetic on it overflows at 32 bits; integer itself is not a column type. NULL is supported.

- `.` `TestDB/round_trips_every_type_through_parameters_and_Scan`: every type and NULL round-trips through $1-style parameters and Scan
- `internal/pgdiff` `TestCasts/every_value_casts_to_every_type_the_same_as_Postgres,_or_is_rejected_as_unsupported`: hegel-drawn values of every supported type, and integer and numeric literals, cast to every supported type and back to text with the same result or error class as Postgres, unless maragudb rejects the cast as unsupported
- `internal/pgdiff` `TestCasts/text_casts_to_every_type,_and_back_to_text,_the_same_as_Postgres,_or_are_rejected_as_unsupported`: hegel-drawn text near valid input for bigint, double precision, boolean, bytea, and timestamptz casts to the type and back to text with the same result or the same error class as Postgres, unless maragudb rejects it as unsupported
- `internal/sql/exec` `TestSession_Insert/applies_Postgres's_assignment_casts`: an INSERT applies the assignment casts Postgres has: a quoted literal as the column's type, numeric and float literals rounded into bigint, integers widened to double precision, and any value written into text
- `internal/sql/exec` `TestSession_Insert/binds_parameters_of_every_type`: every type binds through a parameter, and a timestamptz keeps microseconds
- `internal/sql/exec` `TestSession_Select/evaluates_expressions_like_Postgres`: expressions evaluate as in Postgres: integer literals are 32-bit, numeric literals adapt to double precision, quoted literals take the type their context demands, || writes any type next to text, and casts use Postgres's text formats
- `internal/sql/value` `TestEncodeRow/round_trips_every_type_and_NULL`: every value of the six types and NULL round-trips through the row encoding

### `INV-LOGGER`

> Telemetry: an optional *slog.Logger in Options, plus Stats().

- `internal/engine` `TestOpen/logs_creation_and_commits_to_the_given_logger`: the engine logs database creation and commits to the given slog logger

### `INV-INDEX-CONSISTENT`

> After any committed history, every index holds exactly the entries derived from its table's rows.

- `internal/sim` `TestSimulator/corpus_finds_no_anomalies`: the fixed corpus, with the unique workload under the same faults, finds no two rows with the same unique value in any snapshot a reader saw or in the final state, and after every run through SQL every index of the store matches its table, and lookups through the indexes find the rows of the table
- `internal/sql/exec` `TestMutations_Indexes/IndexStaleDelete_leaves_entries_that_CheckIndexes_finds`: with the mutant, an UPDATE or DELETE leaves its old index entries, which the index check finds
- `internal/sql/exec` `TestSession_ForeignKeysKeepInvariants/random_writes_on_referenced,_referencing,_and_self-referencing_tables_keep_every_foreign_key_and_check,_with_and_without_an_index_on_the_referencing_columns`: random inserts, updates, and deletes, in and out of transactions, on a parent, a child with a random ON DELETE action, and a self-referencing table never leave a row whose foreign key has no parent or a row that violates a CHECK, and a session whose child has an index on its referencing columns gives the same outcomes and rows as one without
- `internal/sql/exec` `TestSession_IndexesMatchModel/random_writes_on_a_table_with_indexes_match_a_model,_and_every_index_matches_its_table_after_every_statement`: random inserts, updates, deletes, and index creations and drops on a table with unique and other indexes give the rows and the unique violations of a model, the indexes match the table after every statement, and lookups through every index return the rows of the model
- `internal/sql/value` `TestEncodeIndexKey/byte_order_of_composite_index_keys_equals_the_order_of_every_column_with_its_direction_and_NULL_placement`: the index key encoding sorts composite keys of every type, ascending or descending, with NULLs first or last, in the order Postgres sorts the index

### `INV-UNIQUE`

> No committed state ever has two rows with equal non-NULL values in a UNIQUE index.

- `internal/pgdiff` `TestIndexes/enforces_UNIQUE_as_Postgres_does,_with_NULLs_distinct_or_not,_and_fails_a_unique_index_on_duplicated_rows`: inserts, updates, and CREATE UNIQUE INDEX that would give two rows the same values of a unique index fail with SQLSTATE 23505 on both, NULLs collide only with NULLS NOT DISTINCT, and the rows are the same on both afterwards
- `internal/pgdiff` `TestIndexes/fails_a_cycle_of_unique_values_in_an_UPDATE_as_Postgres_does_in_every_order,_and_rejects_a_chain`: an UPDATE whose rows swap the values of a unique index or of the primary key fails with SQLSTATE 23505 on both, an UPDATE that moves a chain of rows onto the values the next one leaves is rejected, and one that moves rows onto free values succeeds on both
- `internal/sim` `TestSimulator/corpus_finds_no_anomalies`: the fixed corpus, with the unique workload under the same faults, finds no two rows with the same unique value in any snapshot a reader saw or in the final state, and after every run through SQL every index of the store matches its table, and lookups through the indexes find the rows of the table
- `internal/sql/exec` `TestMutations_Indexes/UniqueNoCheck_and_UniqueOwnWrites_let_duplicates_in`: with either mutant, a unique index lets two rows have the same values, which the index check finds
- `internal/sql/exec` `TestSession_IndexesMatchModel/random_writes_on_a_table_with_indexes_match_a_model,_and_every_index_matches_its_table_after_every_statement`: random inserts, updates, deletes, and index creations and drops on a table with unique and other indexes give the rows and the unique violations of a model, the indexes match the table after every statement, and lookups through every index return the rows of the model
- `internal/sql/exec` `TestSession_Unique/rejects_a_row_whose_values_another_row_has,_in_one_statement_or_across_statements,_and_allows_NULLs`: inserts and updates that would give two rows the same non-NULL values of a unique index fail with ErrDuplicateKey, within one statement, across statements of a transaction, and against committed rows, and NULLs never collide unless NULLS NOT DISTINCT
- `internal/sql/exec` `TestSession_Unique/rejects_an_UPDATE_whose_outcome_depends_on_the_order_Postgres_visits_the_rows,_and_fails_a_cycle_of_moves`: an UPDATE whose rows move onto unique values that other rows of it leave is rejected when they form a chain, whose outcome depends on the order, and fails with ErrDuplicateKey when they form a cycle, which fails in every order

### `INV-CHECK`

> No committed row ever violates a CHECK constraint of its table.

- `internal/pgdiff` `TestChecks/checks_CHECK_constraints_in_the_order_of_their_names,_after_NOT_NULL_and_before_the_keys,_as_Postgres_does`: an INSERT or UPDATE evaluates the NOT NULL constraints, then the CHECK constraints in the order of their names, failing at the first that is false or fails itself, and then the primary key and the unique indexes, row by row, so it fails with the same class as Postgres, and NULL passes a CHECK
- `internal/sim` `TestSimulator/corpus_finds_no_anomalies`: the fixed corpus, with the foreign key workload under the same faults, finds no reference to a missing row and no row that violates a CHECK in any snapshot a reader saw, and after every run through SQL every foreign key and CHECK of the store holds
- `internal/sql/exec` `TestSession_ForeignKeysKeepInvariants/random_writes_on_referenced,_referencing,_and_self-referencing_tables_keep_every_foreign_key_and_check,_with_and_without_an_index_on_the_referencing_columns`: random inserts, updates, and deletes, in and out of transactions, on a parent, a child with a random ON DELETE action, and a self-referencing table never leave a row whose foreign key has no parent or a row that violates a CHECK, and a session whose child has an index on its referencing columns gives the same outcomes and rows as one without

### `INV-FK`

> No committed state ever has a child row whose key has no NULL and no matching parent row (MATCH SIMPLE).

- `internal/pgdiff` `TestForeignKeys/cascades_through_chains_of_tables_and_trees,_and_rejects_actions_whose_outcome_depends_on_their_order`: ON DELETE CASCADE, SET NULL, and SET DEFAULT go through chains of tables and down self-referencing trees as in Postgres, the rows they change are checked like any other, and a DELETE whose actions could give another outcome in another order is rejected
- `internal/pgdiff` `TestForeignKeys/checks_a_self-referencing_table_at_the_end_of_the_statement,_as_Postgres_does`: a self-referencing table is checked at the end of each statement, so an UPDATE that moves parents and children together passes, one that moves only the parents fails, a cycle of references can be inserted in one statement, and deleting a whole tree passes where deleting part of it fails
- `internal/pgdiff` `TestForeignKeys/checks_foreign_keys_and_fires_their_actions_as_Postgres_does`: an insert or update of a row whose foreign key has no NULL and no parent row fails with 23503 at the end of the statement, a delete or key update of a referenced row fails with 23503 for NO ACTION and 23001 for RESTRICT, or deletes, sets to NULL, or sets to the defaults the referencing rows, with the rows the same on both afterwards
- `internal/sim` `TestSimulator/corpus_finds_no_anomalies`: the fixed corpus, with the foreign key workload under the same faults, finds no reference to a missing row and no row that violates a CHECK in any snapshot a reader saw, and after every run through SQL every foreign key and CHECK of the store holds
- `internal/sql/exec` `TestSession_ForeignKeysKeepInvariants/random_writes_on_referenced,_referencing,_and_self-referencing_tables_keep_every_foreign_key_and_check,_with_and_without_an_index_on_the_referencing_columns`: random inserts, updates, and deletes, in and out of transactions, on a parent, a child with a random ON DELETE action, and a self-referencing table never leave a row whose foreign key has no parent or a row that violates a CHECK, and a session whose child has an index on its referencing columns gives the same outcomes and rows as one without

## Unsupported statements

### `UNS-NUMERIC`

> The numeric type.

- `internal/pgdiff` `TestUnsupported/UNS-NUMERIC_numeric_literals_outside_double_precision_and_bigint_contexts`: numeric literals that Postgres keeps as numeric, such as SELECT 1.5 or a literal beyond the bigint range, are rejected, and Postgres accepts them

### `UNS-TYPES`

> Other types.

- `internal/pgdiff` `TestUnsupported/UNS-TYPES_other_types`: type names other than the six supported types and their aliases, and type modifiers, are rejected, and Postgres accepts them

### `UNS-TIMESTAMP-INPUT`

> Timestamps outside ISO 8601 and the common era.

- `internal/pgdiff` `TestUnsupported/UNS-TIMESTAMP-INPUT_timestamps_that_are_not_ISO_8601_or_not_in_the_common_era`: timestamptz text that is not in an ISO 8601 form, special values, named time zones, and instants before year 1 are rejected, and Postgres accepts them

### `UNS-NO-PRIMARY-KEY`

> Tables without a primary key.

- `internal/pgdiff` `TestUnsupported/UNS-NO-PRIMARY-KEY_tables_without_a_primary_key`: a table without a primary key is rejected, and Postgres accepts it

### `UNS-DDL`

> Other schema statements and constraints.

- `internal/pgdiff` `TestUnsupported/UNS-DDL_other_schema_statements_and_constraints`: schema statements other than CREATE TABLE, DROP TABLE, CREATE INDEX, and DROP INDEX, constraints other than PRIMARY KEY, UNIQUE, NOT NULL, DEFAULT, CHECK, and FOREIGN KEY, and a named NOT NULL are rejected, and Postgres accepts them

### `UNS-SEQUENCES`

> Sequences.

- `internal/pgdiff` `TestUnsupported/UNS-SEQUENCES_sequences,_serial_types,_and_identity_columns`: sequences, the serial types, and identity columns are rejected with a hint, and Postgres accepts them

### `UNS-DEFAULT`

> A DEFAULT that can fail.

- `internal/pgdiff` `TestUnsupported/UNS-DEFAULT_a_DEFAULT_that_can_fail`: a DEFAULT whose constant part fails, or that can fail when it is evaluated, is rejected when the table is created, and Postgres accepts the table

### `UNS-CHECK`

> Other forms of CHECK.

- `internal/pgdiff` `TestUnsupported/UNS-CHECK_other_forms_of_CHECK`: a CHECK with NO INHERIT, NOT VALID, or NOT ENFORCED, or whose constant part fails, is rejected, and Postgres accepts the table

### `UNS-FOREIGN-KEY`

> Other forms of FOREIGN KEY.

- `internal/pgdiff` `TestUnsupported/UNS-FOREIGN-KEY_other_forms_of_FOREIGN_KEY`: a foreign key with MATCH FULL, ON UPDATE CASCADE, SET NULL, or SET DEFAULT, NOT VALID, NOT ENFORCED, or DEFERRABLE, or on double precision columns, is rejected, and Postgres accepts the table

### `UNS-INDEX`

> Other forms of indexes.

- `internal/pgdiff` `TestUnsupported/UNS-INDEX_other_forms_of_indexes_and_of_their_constraints`: indexes on expressions, partial indexes, INCLUDE, USING, CONCURRENTLY, ON ONLY, operator classes, COLLATE, storage parameters, tablespaces, ALTER INDEX, several indexes in one DROP INDEX, and DEFERRABLE and NOT DEFERRABLE constraints are rejected, and Postgres accepts them

### `UNS-STATEMENTS`

> Other statements and transaction modes.

- `internal/pgdiff` `TestUnsupported/UNS-STATEMENTS_other_statements_and_transaction_modes`: statements other than CREATE TABLE, DROP TABLE, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, SELECT, and the transaction statements, transaction modes other than SERIALIZABLE, and savepoints are rejected, and Postgres accepts them

### `UNS-CLAUSES`

> Other clauses.

- `internal/pgdiff` `TestUnsupported/UNS-CLAUSES_other_clauses_of_queries_and_writes`: DISTINCT, GROUP BY, joins, subqueries, set operations, aliases, qualified names, FOR UPDATE, RETURNING, ON CONFLICT, and INSERT ... SELECT are rejected, and Postgres accepts them

### `UNS-FUNCTIONS`

> Other functions.

- `internal/pgdiff` `TestUnsupported/UNS-FUNCTIONS_functions_other_than_the_supported_ones`: functions other than abs, coalesce, length, lower, upper, now, transaction_timestamp, and CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, including aggregates, window functions, the other clocks, and CURRENT_TIMESTAMP with a precision, are rejected, and Postgres accepts them

### `UNS-OPERATORS`

> Other operators and predicates.

- `internal/pgdiff` `TestUnsupported/UNS-OPERATORS_other_operators_and_predicates`: operators and predicates other than the supported ones, such as IS DISTINCT FROM, ILIKE, regular expressions, arrays, row constructors, LIKE ... ESCAPE, LIKE on bytea, COLLATE, and AT TIME ZONE, are rejected, and Postgres accepts them

### `UNS-LITERALS`

> Other forms of constants and identifiers.

- `internal/pgdiff` `TestUnsupported/UNS-LITERALS_other_forms_of_constants_and_identifiers`: escape, bit, national, Unicode, and dollar-quoted string constants, strings continued across lines, and non-ASCII unquoted identifiers are rejected, and Postgres accepts them

### `UNS-PARAMETERS`

> A parameter whose Go value would need a conversion.

- `.` `TestDB/gives_a_parameter_the_type_of_its_context,_as_Postgres_does`: a string parameter is read like a quoted literal of the type its context gives it, an int64 converts to a double precision, and a conversion that a Postgres driver might make differently is ErrUnsupported
- `internal/pgdiff` `TestUnsupported/UNS-PARAMETERS_parameters_whose_Go_value_needs_a_conversion`: a parameter whose Go value would have to be converted to the type its context infers, such as a float64 used as a bigint, is rejected, and Postgres with pgx accepts it
- `internal/sql/exec` `TestSession_Select/gives_parameters_the_type_of_their_context`: a parameter of a Go type other than string converts to the type its context infers, overflows like an integer in an integer context, and is ErrUnsupported where it cannot convert

### `UNS-LIMIT-ORDER`

> LIMIT and OFFSET without a total order.

- `internal/pgdiff` `TestUnsupported/UNS-LIMIT-ORDER_LIMIT_and_OFFSET_without_a_total_order`: LIMIT and OFFSET without ORDER BY on every primary key column are rejected, because which rows Postgres returns depends on its plan, and Postgres accepts them
- `internal/sql/exec` `TestSession_Select/rejects_LIMIT_and_OFFSET_whose_rows_or_errors_would_depend_on_Postgres's_plan`: LIMIT and OFFSET need an ORDER BY on every primary key column and no expression that can fail, else ErrUnsupported

### `UNS-PLAN-DEPENDENT-LIMIT`

> LIMIT and OFFSET with an expression that can fail.

- `internal/pgdiff` `TestUnsupported/UNS-PLAN-DEPENDENT-LIMIT_LIMIT_and_OFFSET_with_an_expression_that_can_fail`: LIMIT and OFFSET with an output, ORDER BY, or WHERE expression that can fail are rejected, because how many rows Postgres evaluates it on depends on its plan, and Postgres accepts them when no row fails
- `internal/sql/exec` `TestSession_Select/rejects_LIMIT_and_OFFSET_whose_rows_or_errors_would_depend_on_Postgres's_plan`: LIMIT and OFFSET need an ORDER BY on every primary key column and no expression that can fail, else ErrUnsupported

### `UNS-PLAN-DEPENDENT-WHERE`

> A LIKE on an indexed column whose pattern can fail.

- `internal/pgdiff` `TestUnsupported/UNS-PLAN-DEPENDENT-WHERE_a_LIKE_on_an_indexed_column_whose_pattern_can_fail`: a LIKE on a column of the primary key or of another index whose pattern can fail is rejected, because Postgres scans the index for its prefix and evaluates it only on those rows, and Postgres accepts it when no row there fails
- `internal/sql/exec` `TestSession_Select/accepts_a_WHERE_clause_only_when_its_outcome_is_the_same_in_every_order_Postgres_could_pick_on_the_rows_its_primary_key_index_selects`: a WHERE clause whose outcome on a row depends on the order Postgres evaluates its conditions in, including the equalities its equivalence classes imply, is ErrUnsupported, and so is a LIKE on a key column that can fail; the other conditions are evaluated only on the rows that the primary key conditions select, and every other WHERE clause fails exactly when Postgres fails in every order

### `UNS-ORDER-DEPENDENT-WHERE`

> A condition that fails on a row that another condition rejects.

- `internal/pgdiff` `TestIndexPlans/evaluates_the_other_conditions_only_on_the_rows_that_every_index_scan_Postgres_could_pick_skips,_and_otherwise_on_every_row`: with several indexes, a condition that can fail is evaluated on the rows that any index scan Postgres could pick reads: those of each index's certain conditions, and every row when an index without them could serve a condition or ORDER BY; maragudb gives Postgres's result when every such scan agrees, and rejects the statement otherwise
- `internal/pgdiff` `TestUnsupported/UNS-ORDER-DEPENDENT-WHERE_a_condition_that_fails_on_a_row_that_another_condition_rejects`: a WHERE clause with a condition that fails on a row that another condition rejects is rejected, because whether Postgres fails depends on the order it picks, and Postgres accepts it in the order it picks here
- `internal/sql/exec` `TestSession_Select/accepts_a_WHERE_clause_only_when_its_outcome_is_the_same_in_every_order_Postgres_could_pick_on_the_rows_its_primary_key_index_selects`: a WHERE clause whose outcome on a row depends on the order Postgres evaluates its conditions in, including the equalities its equivalence classes imply, is ErrUnsupported, and so is a LIKE on a key column that can fail; the other conditions are evaluated only on the rows that the primary key conditions select, and every other WHERE clause fails exactly when Postgres fails in every order

### `UNS-STABLE-CONSTANT`

> A conversion between text and timestamptz that reads no columns and can fail.

- `internal/pgdiff` `TestUnsupported/UNS-STABLE-CONSTANT_a_conversion_between_text_and_timestamptz_that_reads_no_columns_and_can_fail`: a conversion between text and timestamptz without columns that can fail is rejected, because whether Postgres evaluates it while planning depends on the plan, and Postgres accepts it when it does not fail
- `internal/sql/exec` `TestSession_Select/does_not_fold_the_stable_conversions_between_timestamptz_and_text,_as_Postgres_does_not,_and_rejects_one_that_can_fail`: a conversion between timestamptz and text is evaluated when the statement runs, so a CASE does not prune on it and a WHERE condition on it is evaluated once before rows are read, and one without columns that can fail is ErrUnsupported

### `UNS-FOREIGN-KEY-ORDER`

> Foreign key actions whose outcome depends on their order.

- `internal/pgdiff` `TestForeignKeys/cascades_through_chains_of_tables_and_trees,_and_rejects_actions_whose_outcome_depends_on_their_order`: ON DELETE CASCADE, SET NULL, and SET DEFAULT go through chains of tables and down self-referencing trees as in Postgres, the rows they change are checked like any other, and a DELETE whose actions could give another outcome in another order is rejected
- `internal/pgdiff` `TestUnsupported/UNS-FOREIGN-KEY-ORDER_a_DELETE_whose_foreign_key_actions_depend_on_their_order`: a DELETE whose foreign key actions could write columns that a check reads, or write a table through more than one foreign key, is rejected, and Postgres accepts it when it fires the actions in the right order

### `UNS-KEY-UPDATE-ORDER`

> An UPDATE that moves a row onto a key that another row leaves.

- `internal/pgdiff` `TestIndexes/fails_a_cycle_of_unique_values_in_an_UPDATE_as_Postgres_does_in_every_order,_and_rejects_a_chain`: an UPDATE whose rows swap the values of a unique index or of the primary key fails with SQLSTATE 23505 on both, an UPDATE that moves a chain of rows onto the values the next one leaves is rejected, and one that moves rows onto free values succeeds on both
- `internal/pgdiff` `TestUnsupported/UNS-KEY-UPDATE-ORDER_an_UPDATE_that_moves_a_key_onto_one_it_moves_away`: an UPDATE that moves a row onto the primary key, or the values of a unique index, of a row that the same statement moves away is rejected, because Postgres checks the key row by row in the order it visits the rows, and Postgres accepts it when it stores the rows in the right order
- `internal/sql/exec` `TestSession_Unique/rejects_an_UPDATE_whose_outcome_depends_on_the_order_Postgres_visits_the_rows,_and_fails_a_cycle_of_moves`: an UPDATE whose rows move onto unique values that other rows of it leave is rejected when they form a chain, whose outcome depends on the order, and fails with ErrDuplicateKey when they form a cycle, which fails in every order
- `internal/sql/exec` `TestSession_Update/moves_rows_when_the_primary_key_changes,_and_rejects_a_move_whose_outcome_depends_on_row_order`: an UPDATE of primary key columns succeeds or fails as in Postgres in every row order, and a chain of rows that move onto keys that other rows move away from is ErrUnsupported, and a cycle of them ErrDuplicateKey

## Remaining differences from Postgres

### `DEV-20`

> A condition that can fail on a row that the primary key does not select.

- `internal/pgdiff` `TestDifferences/DEV-20_Postgres_with_sequential_scans_can_fail_on_a_row_that_the_primary_key_does_not_select`: on a small table with statistics, Postgres in its default configuration scans the whole table and fails on a row that the primary key condition does not select, maragudb evaluates the condition only on the selected rows and succeeds, and Postgres with enable_seqscan=off gives the same result as maragudb

## Mutant kill matrix

Every mutant runs in every simulator configuration below, with seeds 1 to 20, until a checker finds an anomaly. A configuration that never detects a mutant states why it cannot.

| Mutant | Detected in | First seed | Checkers |
|---|---|---|---|
| `MUT-COMMIT-WITHOUT-CAS` commit without CAS | 6 of 12 configurations | 1 | durability, final read, list-append, real-time order |
| `MUT-GC-IGNORE-GRACE` GC ignoring the grace period | 6 of 12 configurations | 1 | final read, grace period, list-append |
| `MUT-SKIP-FRESHNESS` serving the cache without a freshness check | 7 of 12 configurations | 1 | grace period, list-append, real-time order |
| `MUT-ACK-BEFORE-CONFIRM` acking before the write is confirmed | 6 of 12 configurations | 1 | durability, real-time order |
| `MUT-COMPACTED-AHEAD` the compacted segment ahead of newer ones after a rebase | 5 of 12 configurations | 1 | durability, index consistency, list-append, real-time order |
| `MUT-FRESH-SNAPSHOT` a fresh snapshot per statement | 8 of 8 configurations | 1 | bank, foreign key, index consistency, list-append |
| `MUT-RETRY-UNKNOWN` retrying an autocommit statement after an unknown commit outcome | 2 of 8 configurations | 1 | durability, list-append |
| `MUT-INDEX-STALE-DELETE` stale index entries after an UPDATE or DELETE | 6 of 8 configurations | 1 | index consistency |
| `MUT-UNIQUE-NO-CHECK` no unique check | 2 of 8 configurations | 1 | index consistency, unique |
| `MUT-UNIQUE-OWN-WRITES` a unique check that misses the statement's own writes | 2 of 8 configurations | 5 | index consistency, unique |
| `MUT-FK-NO-CHILD-CHECK` no check of a referencing row | 2 of 8 configurations | 1 | foreign key |
| `MUT-FK-NO-PARENT-CHECK` no check or action on the referencing rows | 2 of 8 configurations | 1 | foreign key |
| `MUT-FK-OWN-WRITES` foreign key lookups that miss the statement's own writes | 2 of 8 configurations | 1 | foreign key |
| `MUT-CHECK-SKIP-UPDATE` CHECK on INSERT only | 2 of 8 configurations | 1 | check constraint |
| `MUT-UPDATE-SEES-OWN-WRITES` an UPDATE that revisits the rows it wrote | 0 of 8 configurations | none |  |

### `MUT-COMMIT-WITHOUT-CAS`

`engine.Mutations.CommitWithoutCAS` writes the manifest unconditionally, so a commit can overwrite a concurrent one.

| Configuration | Result |
|---|---|
| list-append through the engine, no maintainers | detected with seed 1 by durability, list-append |
| list-append through the engine, 2 maintainers | detected with seed 1 by durability, list-append |
| bank through the engine, no maintainers | cannot detect: an unconditional manifest write drops whole concurrent commits, a dropped transfer conserves money, and the bank checker only checks totals |
| bank through the engine, 2 maintainers | cannot detect: an unconditional manifest write drops whole concurrent commits, a dropped transfer conserves money, and the bank checker only checks totals |
| list-append through SQL, no maintainers | detected with seed 1 by final read, list-append |
| list-append through SQL, 2 maintainers | detected with seed 1 by durability, list-append |
| bank through SQL, no maintainers | cannot detect: an unconditional manifest write drops whole concurrent commits, a dropped transfer conserves money, and the bank checker only checks totals |
| bank through SQL, 2 maintainers | cannot detect: an unconditional manifest write drops whole concurrent commits, a dropped transfer conserves money, and the bank checker only checks totals |
| unique through SQL, no maintainers | cannot detect: an unconditional manifest write drops whole concurrent commits, which leaves a consistent state in which no value repeats, and the unique workload does not check that acknowledged writes survive |
| unique through SQL, 2 maintainers | cannot detect: an unconditional manifest write drops whole concurrent commits, which leaves a consistent state in which no value repeats, and the unique workload does not check that acknowledged writes survive |
| foreign-key through SQL, no maintainers | detected with seed 1 by real-time order |
| foreign-key through SQL, 2 maintainers | detected with seed 3 by real-time order |

Targeted tests:

- `internal/engine` `TestMutations/CommitWithoutCAS_lets_a_stale_commit_overwrite_a_newer_one`: with the mutant, a stale commit overwrites another process's newer commit
- `internal/workload` `TestRun/finds_the_lost_writes_of_a_commit_without_CAS`: the real-store workload's checkers find the lost writes of the mutant

### `MUT-GC-IGNORE-GRACE`

`engine.Mutations.GCIgnoreGrace` deletes unreferenced objects at once, so a reader younger than the grace period can lose its snapshot.

| Configuration | Result |
|---|---|
| list-append through the engine, no maintainers | cannot detect: without maintainers nothing is ever deleted, so no reader can lose an object |
| list-append through the engine, 2 maintainers | detected with seed 1 by final read, list-append |
| bank through the engine, no maintainers | cannot detect: without maintainers nothing is ever deleted, so no reader can lose an object |
| bank through the engine, 2 maintainers | detected with seed 2 by grace period |
| list-append through SQL, no maintainers | cannot detect: without maintainers nothing is ever deleted, so no reader can lose an object |
| list-append through SQL, 2 maintainers | detected with seed 2 by grace period, final read, list-append |
| bank through SQL, no maintainers | cannot detect: without maintainers nothing is ever deleted, so no reader can lose an object |
| bank through SQL, 2 maintainers | detected with seed 2 by grace period |
| unique through SQL, no maintainers | cannot detect: without maintainers nothing is ever deleted, so no reader can lose an object |
| unique through SQL, 2 maintainers | detected with seed 1 by grace period |
| foreign-key through SQL, no maintainers | cannot detect: without maintainers nothing is ever deleted, so no reader can lose an object |
| foreign-key through SQL, 2 maintainers | detected with seed 1 by grace period |

Targeted tests:

- `internal/workload` `TestRun/finds_snapshots_lost_before_the_grace_period_ends,_when_GC_ignores_it`: the real-store workload finds snapshots lost early with the mutant

### `MUT-SKIP-FRESHNESS`

`engine.Mutations.SkipFreshnessCheck` starts transactions from the cached manifest without asking the store, so a transaction can miss commits acknowledged before it began.

| Configuration | Result |
|---|---|
| list-append through the engine, no maintainers | detected with seed 1 by list-append |
| list-append through the engine, 2 maintainers | detected with seed 1 by list-append |
| bank through the engine, no maintainers | cannot detect: a stale snapshot makes a transfer conflict or read an older consistent state, which conserves money |
| bank through the engine, 2 maintainers | cannot detect: a stale snapshot makes a transfer conflict or read an older consistent state, which conserves money |
| list-append through SQL, no maintainers | detected with seed 1 by list-append |
| list-append through SQL, 2 maintainers | detected with seed 1 by list-append |
| bank through SQL, no maintainers | cannot detect: a stale snapshot makes a transfer conflict or read an older consistent state, which conserves money |
| bank through SQL, 2 maintainers | cannot detect: a stale snapshot makes a transfer conflict or read an older consistent state, which conserves money |
| unique through SQL, no maintainers | cannot detect: a stale snapshot is an older consistent state in which no value repeats, and a write from it conflicts at commit; without maintainers no reader loses an object either |
| unique through SQL, 2 maintainers | detected with seed 5 by grace period |
| foreign-key through SQL, no maintainers | detected with seed 2 by real-time order |
| foreign-key through SQL, 2 maintainers | detected with seed 1 by real-time order |

### `MUT-ACK-BEFORE-CONFIRM`

`engine.Mutations.AckBeforeConfirm` reports a commit as successful without waiting for the store's answer.

| Configuration | Result |
|---|---|
| list-append through the engine, no maintainers | detected with seed 1 by durability |
| list-append through the engine, 2 maintainers | detected with seed 1 by durability |
| bank through the engine, no maintainers | cannot detect: an acknowledged transfer that never landed is missing as a whole, which conserves money |
| bank through the engine, 2 maintainers | cannot detect: an acknowledged transfer that never landed is missing as a whole, which conserves money |
| list-append through SQL, no maintainers | detected with seed 1 by durability |
| list-append through SQL, 2 maintainers | detected with seed 1 by durability |
| bank through SQL, no maintainers | cannot detect: an acknowledged transfer that never landed is missing as a whole, which conserves money |
| bank through SQL, 2 maintainers | cannot detect: an acknowledged transfer that never landed is missing as a whole, which conserves money |
| unique through SQL, no maintainers | cannot detect: an acknowledged write that never landed is missing as a whole, which leaves a consistent state, and the unique workload does not check that acknowledged writes survive |
| unique through SQL, 2 maintainers | cannot detect: an acknowledged write that never landed is missing as a whole, which leaves a consistent state, and the unique workload does not check that acknowledged writes survive |
| foreign-key through SQL, no maintainers | detected with seed 2 by real-time order |
| foreign-key through SQL, 2 maintainers | detected with seed 2 by real-time order |

Targeted tests:

- `internal/engine` `TestMutations/AckBeforeConfirm_reports_success_for_a_write_that_never_happened`: with the mutant, a commit whose manifest write failed is reported as successful and is invisible

### `MUT-COMPACTED-AHEAD`

`engine.Mutations.CompactedSegmentAhead` puts the compacted segment ahead of the segments committed during the compaction when it rebases, so that old values shadow newer ones.

| Configuration | Result |
|---|---|
| list-append through the engine, no maintainers | cannot detect: without maintainers nothing compacts, so there is never a rebase |
| list-append through the engine, 2 maintainers | detected with seed 1 by durability, list-append |
| bank through the engine, no maintainers | cannot detect: without maintainers nothing compacts, so there is never a rebase |
| bank through the engine, 2 maintainers | cannot detect: resurrected balances are a consistent older state, which conserves money, and the engine workload has no index |
| list-append through SQL, no maintainers | cannot detect: without maintainers nothing compacts, so there is never a rebase |
| list-append through SQL, 2 maintainers | detected with seed 1 by durability, list-append |
| bank through SQL, no maintainers | cannot detect: without maintainers nothing compacts, so there is never a rebase |
| bank through SQL, 2 maintainers | detected with seed 2 by index consistency |
| unique through SQL, no maintainers | cannot detect: without maintainers nothing compacts, so there is never a rebase |
| unique through SQL, 2 maintainers | detected with seed 2 by index consistency |
| foreign-key through SQL, no maintainers | cannot detect: without maintainers nothing compacts, so there is never a rebase |
| foreign-key through SQL, 2 maintainers | detected with seed 3 by real-time order |

Targeted tests:

- `internal/engine` `TestMutations/CompactedSegmentAhead_lets_a_rebased_compaction_hide_newer_commits`: with the mutant, a rebased compaction resurrects values that a newer commit deleted and changed

### `MUT-RETRY-UNKNOWN`

`exec.Mutations.RetryAfterUnknownCommit` retries an autocommit statement whose commit outcome is unknown, which can apply it twice.

| Configuration | Result |
|---|---|
| list-append through the engine, no maintainers | not applicable: the mutant is in the SQL layer, which the engine workloads do not use |
| list-append through the engine, 2 maintainers | not applicable: the mutant is in the SQL layer, which the engine workloads do not use |
| bank through the engine, no maintainers | not applicable: the mutant is in the SQL layer, which the engine workloads do not use |
| bank through the engine, 2 maintainers | not applicable: the mutant is in the SQL layer, which the engine workloads do not use |
| list-append through SQL, no maintainers | detected with seed 1 by durability, list-append |
| list-append through SQL, 2 maintainers | detected with seed 2 by durability, list-append |
| bank through SQL, no maintainers | cannot detect: the bank workload writes only in explicit transactions, so no autocommit statement is ever retried, and a doubled transfer conserves money anyway |
| bank through SQL, 2 maintainers | cannot detect: the bank workload writes only in explicit transactions, so no autocommit statement is ever retried, and a doubled transfer conserves money anyway |
| unique through SQL, no maintainers | cannot detect: a retried insert fails on its own primary key, and a retried move or delete finds its row moved or gone, so a statement applied twice leaves a consistent state |
| unique through SQL, 2 maintainers | cannot detect: a retried insert fails on its own primary key, and a retried move or delete finds its row moved or gone, so a statement applied twice leaves a consistent state |
| foreign-key through SQL, no maintainers | cannot detect: a retried statement is checked again against every foreign key and check, so even one applied twice, such as an increment, leaves a consistent state, and the counter is incremented only in transactions, which are never retried |
| foreign-key through SQL, 2 maintainers | cannot detect: a retried statement is checked again against every foreign key and check, so even one applied twice, such as an increment, leaves a consistent state, and the counter is incremented only in transactions, which are never retried |

Targeted tests:

- `internal/sql/exec` `TestMutations/RetryAfterUnknownCommit_applies_a_statement_twice`: with the mutant, an autocommit UPDATE whose outcome was unknown is applied twice

`exec.Mutations.UpdateSeesOwnWrites` restarts an UPDATE's scan after every row it writes, the Halloween problem. It only shows when an UPDATE moves rows to keys it has not visited yet.

## Reached states

The fixed simulator corpus must reach every state at least once, or its test fails. The counts of each run are in the CI report.

| ID | State | Antithesis assertion |
|---|---|---|
| `STATE-LOST-ACK-LANDED` | a manifest write whose answer was lost is resolved as landed | "a lost manifest write is found to have landed" |
| `STATE-LOST-ACK-CONFLICT` | a manifest write without a definite answer, from a lost acknowledgement or a failed request, is resolved as a conflict, because another commit took its sequence number | "a lost manifest write is found to have lost to a concurrent commit" |
| `STATE-LIVE-UNKNOWN` | a commit outcome is unknown in a client process that did not crash | "a commit outcome is unknown in a process that keeps running" |
| `STATE-AUTOCOMMIT-RETRY` | an autocommit statement retries after a conflict | "an autocommit statement retries after a conflict" |
| `STATE-COMPACTION-REBASE` | a compaction reapplies its swap on top of commits that landed meanwhile | "a compaction rebases on commits that only added segments" |
| `STATE-GC-REBASE` | a GC pass reapplies its manifest change on top of commits that landed meanwhile | "a GC pass rebases on commits that landed meanwhile" |
| `STATE-LEASE-TAKEOVER` | a maintainer takes over a lease that another holder let expire | "a maintainer takes over an expired lease" |
| `STATE-LEASE-OVERLAP` | two maintainers believe they hold the lease at the same time | "two maintainers believe they hold the lease at once" |
| `STATE-SNAPSHOT-EXPIRED-REFUSED` | a reader older than the grace period is refused with ErrSnapshotExpired | "a reader older than the grace period is told so" |
| `STATE-BLOCK-READ-RETRY-SUCCEEDED` | a block read that failed transiently is retried and then succeeds | "a retried block read succeeds" |
| `STATE-CRASH-MID-COMMIT-RECOVERED` | a client crashes in the middle of a commit, restarts, and commits again | "a client that crashed during a commit recovers and commits" |
| `STATE-CRASH-MID-COMPACTION` | a process crashes in the middle of a compaction | "a process crashes during a compaction" |
| `STATE-CRASH-MID-GC` | a process crashes in the middle of a GC pass | "a process crashes during a GC pass" |
| `STATE-UNIQUE-AFTER-CONFLICT` | an autocommit statement that passed its unique checks loses its commit to a concurrent one, and its retry fails with a unique violation that the concurrent commit causes | "a unique violation occurs only because of a concurrent commit" |
| `STATE-UNIQUE-VALUE-REUSED` | a client inserts a row with a unique value that its own committed UPDATE or DELETE freed | "a unique value that a committed write freed is taken again" |
| `STATE-FK-AFTER-CONFLICT` | an autocommit statement that passed its foreign key checks loses its commit to a concurrent one, and its retry fails with a foreign key violation that the concurrent commit causes | "a foreign key violation occurs only because of a concurrent commit" |
| `STATE-FK-CASCADE-TABLES` | one statement's ON DELETE CASCADE actions delete rows in more than one table | "a cascade deletes rows in more than one table" |

Verified by:

- `internal/sim` `TestSimulator/corpus_finds_no_anomalies`: the fixed corpus reaches every declared state at least once, among them crashes during commits, compactions, and GC passes, lost acknowledgements resolved both ways, and unique and foreign key violations that only a concurrent commit causes
